name: Occult Macular Dystrophy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Occult Macular Dystrophy

criteria.description: Progressive bilateral central visual acuity loss with normal fundus appearance
Normal fluorescein angiography findings despite visual loss
Reduced macular function demonstrated by multifocal electroretinography (mfERG)
Disruption or loss of photoreceptor inner segment/outer segment junction on OCT
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive bilateral central visual acuity loss with normal fundus and fluorescein angiography, plus reduced macular function on mfERG
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other macular dystrophies and retinal diseases.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bilateral progressive central visual acuity loss
searchTerms: gradual loss of sharp central vision in both eyes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Normal fundus appearance despite visual impairment
searchTerms: normal eye back appearance despite poor vision
healthy retina look with vision loss
no visible eye damage but vision impaired

pathognomonic.symptomName: Reduced macular response on multifocal electroretinography
searchTerms: decreased response in central retina tests
weak macular function on eye tests
reduced retinal electrical activity in macula

common.symptomName: Photoreceptor inner segment/outer segment junction disruption on OCT
searchTerms: damage to light-sensing cell layers in retina
disruption in photoreceptor layers seen on imaging

common.symptomName: Difficulty with reading and recognizing faces
Central scotoma on visual field testing
searchTerms: blind spot in center of vision
dark spot in middle of sight
no abnormalities on fluorescein eye test
slightly reduced ability to see contrast

imaging: Optical coherence tomography showing photoreceptor layer disruption
Normal fundus autofluorescence or mild abnormalities
genetic: Mutations in RP1L1 gene associated with autosomal dominant inheritance
other: Reduced macular response on multifocal electroretinography (mfERG)

distinguishingFeatures: Fundus flecks and atrophy visible on examination
Bone spicule pigmentation on fundus exam
Night blindness as an early symptom
Drusen deposits visible on fundus exam
Progressive central vision loss with fundus abnormalities

redFlags: Presence of fundus abnormalities inconsistent with OMD
references: Miyake Y et al. Occult Macular Dystrophy: Clinical and Genetic Features. Prog Retin Eye Res. 2019.
Kondo M et al. RP1L1 mutations in Occult Macular Dystrophy. Am J Ophthalmol. 2015.
